summary: Finalized the concrete system/component structure for FEAT-1 by folding architecture-critic's two round-2 advisory findings (AC-5, AC-6) into the design before code generation begins at stage 3.5, per architecture-critic's own 'open_items' note. This stage is design-only per system-engineer.md's scope (component boundaries, data flow, schema, caching) — no application code was created or edited; code generation starts at 3.5 (Engineer/MVP). No database schema or caching strategy applies to this feature (pure frontend, no persistence, no network cache beyond the existing useMasterDataTable fetch, which is unchanged).

AC-5_resolution.finding: SDD had AppShell resolving useCurrentUser() and passing a `user` prop into TopBar, but TopBar's role text renders UserBadge (which self-fetches via its own useCurrentUser() call and takes no props) — so TopBar's `user` prop would be dead/unused, and the mock user gets fetched twice through two different paths.
AC-5_resolution.decision: Accepted architecture-critic's recommendation verbatim. TopBar takes only `title: PropTypes.string.isRequired` and renders `<UserBadge />` directly with no `user` prop. AppShell does NOT call useCurrentUser() itself and does NOT pass a user prop down through TopBar — UserBadge is the single call site for useCurrentUser() in the whole tree.

AppShell.note: AppShell's responsibility for user context is removed entirely — it no longer knows or cares about the current user. This also simplifies AppShell's own state/prop surface, directly addressing tech-lead's flagged 'AppShell god-component' risk by keeping one more concern (user identity) out of it.

AC-5_resolution.data_flow_update: UserBadge -> useCurrentUser() -> MOCK_CURRENT_USER. This is now the ONLY path any component reaches user data through. AppShell -> TopBar -> UserBadge carries no user data as props at all.

AC-6_resolution.finding: SDD's supporting_modules placed the mock user data file at a new top-level `src/mock/currentUser.js`, deviating without explicit call-out from tech-lead's literal hard-constraint path `src/lib/currentUser.js` and from the repo's documented directory map.
AC-6_resolution.decision: Accepted architecture-critic's recommendation: keep the file/hook split (it matches the existing masterDataApi.js + useMasterDataTable.js idiom) but relocate the mock-data file under `src/lib/` instead of a new top-level `src/mock/` directory. No new top-level source directory is introduced by this feature.

final_file_layout.src/lib/currentUser.js: Exports MOCK_CURRENT_USER = { id, name, role, initials }. No token, no email persistence, no auth call. A fictitious placeholder identity, not any real person's data.
final_file_layout.src/hooks/useCurrentUser.js: Imports MOCK_CURRENT_USER from '../lib/currentUser' and returns it as-is: { id, name, role, initials }. This hook is the single seam future real-auth work replaces; every consumer goes through it, never src/lib/currentUser.js directly.

final_component_breakdown.role: Top-level internal-app container. Renders Sidebar + TopBar + a content outlet. Owns activeViewId as local useState, derived from an initialHash prop on mount via NAV_ITEMS lookup (fallback: NAV_ITEMS[0].id).

state.activeViewId: string — id of the entry in NAV_ITEMS currently shown in the content outlet

children_rendered: the active NAV_ITEMS entry's component (MasterDataView for id 'master-data')

final_component_breakdown.role: Persistent left nav. Pure presentational list of NAV_ITEMS, highlights activeId, calls onSelect(id) on click. No routing/hash knowledge — AppShell owns that. Unchanged from SDD.
Workspace chrome bar: current section title (derived by AppShell from the active NAV_ITEMS entry's label) on the left + UserBadge on the right. Purely presentational.
final_component_breakdown.changed_from_sdd: Dropped the `user` shape prop per AC-5_resolution — was dead/unused and caused a double-fetch path.

final_component_breakdown.role: Signed-in-user chip: initials avatar + name + role. Calls useCurrentUser() itself — the single call site in the tree — so any consumer can drop it in without prop drilling the mock user.

final_supporting_modules.role: Single explicitly-named mock export, MOCK_CURRENT_USER = { id, name, role, initials }. Relocated from src/mock/currentUser.js per AC-6_resolution — matches tech-lead's literal hard-constraint path and the repo's existing top-level directory map (no new top-level dir).
Returns MOCK_CURRENT_USER as-is: { id, name, role, initials }. The single seam future real-auth work replaces. Only UserBadge calls it, per AC-5_resolution.

NAV_ITEMS registry: [{ id: 'master-data', label: 'Master Data', hash: '#master-data', component: MasterDataView }]. Single array AppShell/Sidebar both read. Also exports APP_SHELL_HASHES (derived from NAV_ITEMS) so App.jsx and AppShell can't drift out of sync. Unchanged from SDD.

final_data_flow: App.jsx reads hash via useLocationHash (unchanged hook).

App.jsx: APP_SHELL_HASHES.includes(hash) ? <AppShell initialHash={hash} /> : <Header/><main>Hero/ServicesSection/DeliveryCenters</main><Footer/> — single outermost ternary, per SDD round 2 / AC-1 fix. Verified against the current, unmodified src/App.jsx.
AppShell resolves initialHash -> activeViewId via NAV_ITEMS lookup (fallback: NAV_ITEMS[0].id).
AppShell renders TopBar(title=<active item's label>) — no user prop (AC-5_resolution). TopBar renders <UserBadge/> internally.
UserBadge calls useCurrentUser() -> reads src/lib/currentUser.js's MOCK_CURRENT_USER (AC-6_resolution) -> renders initials/name/role.

AppShell renders the active NAV_ITEMS entry's component in the content outlet (MasterDataView today) — MasterDataView's own internal state (tabs, table data fetching via useMasterDataTable) is untouched.
database_schema: Not applicable — no backend/database exists in this project yet (CLAUDE.md §0, §11 forward-looking only). This feature is pure frontend composition over the existing useMasterDataTable fetch layer, which is unmodified.
caching_strategy: Not applicable — no new network calls are introduced. useMasterDataTable's existing fetch-on-mount behavior (with its cancelled-flag cleanup guard) is reused unchanged; MOCK_CURRENT_USER is a static in-memory module export, not a fetched or cached value.

propTypes_plan.Sidebar: items: PropTypes.arrayOf(PropTypes.shape({ id: PropTypes.string.isRequired, label: PropTypes.string.isRequired })).isRequired, activeId: PropTypes.string.isRequired, onSelect: PropTypes.func.isRequired
propTypes_plan.TopBar: title: PropTypes.string.isRequired  (user shape prop removed per AC-5_resolution)

constraints_carried_forward_unchanged: No new router/UI-kit/state-management dependency; prop-types remains the one explicitly-justified exception (SDD dependency_decision).
Marketing components remain untouched and decoupled; App.jsx's single outermost hash ternary is the only branch point (AC-1 fix, re-verified against current App.jsx).
One component per folder, CSS Modules, camelCase classes, additive-only design tokens (--shell-sidebar-width, --shell-topbar-height) in src/index.css :root.
PropTypes required on every new component.
Internal nav (Sidebar clicks) is plain useState, not hash-addressable past the entry hash — accepted trade-off (SDD/AC-3).
open_items_for_engineer_mvp: Stage 3.5 builds AppShell, Sidebar, TopBar, UserBadge, src/lib/navigation.js, src/lib/currentUser.js, src/hooks/useCurrentUser.js exactly per this stage's final_component_breakdown / final_supporting_modules / final_data_flow — no further redesign needed for AC-5/AC-6, both are now closed.
